meta.gate_note: 방구석 전용 게이트 A(얼굴=나 같은 사람 40대 후반~50대 초반) · B(원 단위 금액 물리적 존재) · C(사건 진행중) · D(주어=내 돈) 9장 전부 통과. 좌우 대비 3장(1·5·6) 확보. 한글+영문 2단 간판 2장(2·6). 종목명·증권사 로고·하락 차트·빨간 마이너스는 전 장 배제 — 이 편의 감정은 손실 경악이 아니라 '이게 나였다고?' 놀람+안도다.
meta.prompt_suffix: SCREEN RULE: any phone or monitor screen in this frame is a light source, not a dark slab — a bright, near-white interface that is the brightest rectangle in the picture, never switched off, never a black screen, never showing a blinking cursor bar. LETTERING RULE: only the surfaces that were given a quoted phrase above carry any lettering at all. Every other badge, ribbon, medal, signboard, poster, notice, sheet of paper, book spine, box, label and screen in the frame is completely BLANK — clean unmarked material with no characters on it. A blank surface is a correct result; an invented or half-formed word is a failure. NUMBER RULE, applies to every number in this image: each amount is drawn exactly as quoted above, in the short Korean unit form, and always sits on ONE unbroken line. Never wrap a number onto a second line, never split it in the middle of a digit group, never let a comma fall at the end of a line. If an amount would not fit across the surface it sits on, draw the amount smaller — never break it. Style: candid documentary photograph of a real place, not an advertisement, not CGI, not a composite. Shot on a full-frame camera with a 35mm lens at about f/2.8, standing eye level, available light only, true-to-life restrained colour, mild sensor noise, a slight handheld tilt, honest texture on skin, wood, glass and metal. Screens, boards and signs carry their own backlight because they really do, but nothing else glows — never hyper-saturated, no HDR look, no rim-light effects, no lens flare, no graphic arrows, no highlight circles, no cracks or sparks. No title overlay text, no captions, no subtitle bars, no large lettering across the frame, no watermark. Apart from the Korean words and digits named above, do not invent any other lettering anywhere in the image — no English text, no latin letters, no fake Chinese characters, no gibberish text, no random lettering, no invented words; every other printed surface is too small and slightly out of focus to read. No brand logos, no company names, no stock ticker names anywhere.

thumbnails.concept_ko: 한 줄: '같은 방 안에서 열 명 중 여섯의 잔고와 내 잔고가 나란히 걸려 있다.' 파트 1(1,000만 미만 876만 명=열 명 중 여섯, 1인당 230만 원 vs 1억)이 근거. [A 얼굴] 나 같은 사람(50대 초반 월급쟁이 · 40대 후반 직장인) [B 금액] "2,300,000원" / "1억 원" [C 사건] 오른쪽 남자가 폰을 막 내리며 고개를 드는 순간, 보드 숫자가 방금 갱신됨 [D 주어] 갈린 두 잔고가 둘 다 내 계좌 이야기다 [구도] 좌우대비 [텍스트] 제목「이 줄에 서 계십니다」 vs 썸네일「열 명 세우면 나오는 자리」
thumbnails.prompt_en: COMPOSITION RULE, HIGHEST PRIORITY: the photograph fills the entire 16:9 frame edge to edge with a real scene — never a letterbox band, never an empty panel, never a flat colour block, and never a large expanse of bare empty floor. The bottom three-eighths of the frame height is filled by the dark backs and shoulders of the people nearest the camera, so far out of focus and so deeply in shadow that it reads as one single dark mass with no readable detail, which keeps overlay text legible on top of it. No face, no hand, no screen and no bright object sits in that bottom three-eighths — every face, hand, sign and key object sits in the upper five-eighths. Counters and table tops run across the MIDDLE of the frame, never near the bottom edge, and anything resting on them sits at mid height. SCALE, EQUALLY IMPORTANT: the two Korean men are by far the largest things in the picture — each of them occupies his own half of the frame, each face alone spans roughly the top forty-five to fifty percent of the frame height, the top of each man's hair touches the upper edge and is very slightly cropped by it, and their outer shoulders leave the frame on the left and on the right. Every other person in the room is far smaller, roughly one third of their head height. Scene: the waiting hall of a Korean securities branch office at midday, photographed from inside at standing eye level. A floor-to-ceiling glass partition column runs straight down the exact middle of the frame and splits it into two halves. On the left half, a Korean man in his early fifties in a worn grey zip-up jacket sits slightly lower; on the wall above him a large flat wall monitor turned to face the camera shows the Korean word "평가금액" in Korean Hangul on its top line and the figure "230만 원" beneath it in plain white digits. On the right half, a Korean man in his late forties in an open-collar shirt stands, having just lowered the phone in his hand; the identical monitor on his side shows "평가금액" in Korean Hangul and "1억 원" beneath it. Both boards are turned squarely toward the lens and the digits are huge — each character about one twelfth of the frame height and filling most of the board width — and the small ticker row under them is caught mid-refresh, half the row still changing. Expressions are opposite: the left man's eyes are cast down, lips pressed tight, shoulders sunk, one hand loose on his knee; the right man's eyebrows are lifted high, his mouth is half open, and one hand has frozen halfway up to his chest as if he has just recognised something about himself. Warm ceiling fluorescent light inside mixes with cooler daylight from the street window behind them; scuffed floor, a stack of paper leaflets curling at the corner on the counter, worn vinyl chairs, tangled cabling under the desk.
